This result is consistent with the systematic trend of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> estimates based on galactic SFR indicators at different wavelengths (ultraviolet, H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex>, and infrared), indicating that there is a strong evolution in the mean extinction of star-forming regions in galaxies at relatively low redshift range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \lesssim$</tex>0.5. These results are obtained by a method that is completely independent of galaxy surveys and, especially, there is no detection limit about the host galaxy luminosity in our analysis, giving a strong constraint on the star-formation activity in high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> dwarf galaxies or intergalactic space.

articleTitle: Subaru/MOIRCS Near-Infrared Imaging in the Proto-Cluster Region at z = 3.1
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the results of deep near-infrared imaging observations of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z=3.1$</tex> proto-cluster region in the SSA 22a field taken by MOIRCS mounted on the Subaru Telescope. We observed a 21.7 arcmin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> field to depths of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J=$</tex> 24.5, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H=$</tex> 24.3, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K=$</tex> 23.9 (5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex>). We examined the distribution of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-selected galaxies at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \sim 3$</tex> by using a simple color cut for distant red galaxies (DRGs) as well as a photometric-redshift selection technique. The marginal density excess of DRGs and the photo-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> selected objects were found around the two most luminous Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> blobs (LABs). We investigated the correlation between the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-selected objects and the LABs, and found that several galaxies with stellar mass, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_* = 10^{9}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{11} M_\odot$</tex>, exist in the vicinity of LABs, especially around the two most luminous ones. We also found that 7 of the 8LABs in the field have plausible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{\rm s}$</tex>-band counterparts, and the sum of the stellar mass possibly associated with LABs correlates with their luminosity and surface brightness, which implies that the origin of Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission may be closely correlated with their previous star-formation phenomena.

articleTitle: Suzaku Wide-Band Observations of SN 1006
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the wide-band spectra of SN1006, as observed by Suzaku. Thermal and nonthermal emissions were successfully resolved thanks to the excellent spectral response of Suzaku's X-ray CCD XIS. The nonthermal emission could not be reproduced by a simple power-law model, but needed a roll-off at 5.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{16}$</tex>Hz = 0.23keV. The roll-off frequency is significantly higher in the northeastern rim than in the southwestern rim. We also placed the most stringent upper limit of the flux above 10keV using the Hard X-ray Detector.

articleTitle: Suzaku Spectroscopy of an X-Ray Reflection Nebula and a New Supernova Remnant Candidate in the SgrB1 Region
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We made a 100 ks observation of the Sagittarius (Sgr) B1 region at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(l,\ b)=$</tex> (0D.5, -0D.1) near to the Galactic center (GC) with the Suzaku/XIS. Emission lines of SXV, FeI, FeXXV, and FeXXVI were clearly detected in the spectrum. We found that the FeXXV and FeXXVI line emissions smoothly distribute over the SgrB1 and B2 regions connecting from the GC. This result suggests that the GC hot plasma extends at least up to the SgrB region with constant temperature. There are two diffuse X-ray sources in the observed region. One of the two (G0.42-0.04) is newly discovered, and exhibits a strong SXV K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> emission line, suggesting a candidate for a supernova remnant located in the GC region. The other one (M0.51-0.10), having a prominent FeI K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> emission line and a strongly absorbed continuum, is likely to be an X-ray reflection nebula. There is no near source bright enough to irradiate M0.51-0.10. However, the FeI K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> emission can be explained if SgrA* was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim10^6$</tex> times brighter 300years ago, the light travel time for 100 pc to M0.51-0.10, than it is at present.

articleTitle: Planetary Companions to Evolved Intermediate-Mass Stars: 14 Andromedae, 81 Ceti, 6 Lyncis, and HD167042
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the detection of four extrasolar planets orbiting evolved intermediate-mass stars from a precise Doppler survey of G-K giants at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory. All of the host stars are considered to be formerly early F-type or A-type dwarfs when they were on the main sequence. 14 And (K0 III) is a clump giant with a mass of 2.2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\odot}$</tex> and has a planet of minimum mass <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_2$</tex>sin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>= 4.8<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\rm J}$</tex> in a nearly circular orbit with a 186d period. This is one of the innermost planets around evolved intermediate-mass stars, and such planets have only been discovered in clump giants. 81 Cet (G5 III) is a clump giant with 2.4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\odot}$</tex> hosting a planet of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_2$</tex>sin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>= 5.3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\rm J}$</tex> in a 953d orbit with an eccentricity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e=$</tex> 0.21. 6 Lyn (K0 IV) is a less-evolved subgiant with 1.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\odot}$</tex>, and has a planet of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_2$</tex>sin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>= 2.4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\rm J}$</tex> in a 899d orbit with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e=$</tex> 0.13. HD167042 (K1 IV) is also a less-evolved star with 1.5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\odot}$</tex> hosting a planet of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_2$</tex>sin<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>= 1.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{\rm J}$</tex> in a 418d orbit with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e=$</tex> 0.10. This planet was independently announced by Johnson et al. (2008, ApJ, 675, 784). All of the host stars have solar or sub-solar metallicity, which supports the lack of a metal-rich tendency in planet-harboring giants in contrast to the case of dwarfs.

articleTitle: Slit-Modulation Imaging Method for Detecting Any Periodic Structural Change in Interferometric Data
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We propose a slit-modulation imaging (SMI) method, a new imaging technique for detecting shorter periodic structural changes of interferometric data. Using simulations with artificial visibility data, we show that the SMI method is highly effective in detecting periodic change patterns, of which period is shorter than the observing time span, of interferometric data.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Spectra of 21 Wolf–Rayet Stars: Wind Clumping and Mass-Loss Rates
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present 0.9–2.4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m spectra of 21 galactic Wolf–Rayet (WR) stars that were obtained by using an echelle spectrograph attached to the 1.5 m infrared telescope in Tokyo. The observed Wolf–Rayet stars contain 12WNE, 3WNL, and 6WC stars. The near-infrared continuum spectra can be fitted by the superposition of stellar blackbody radiation with a stellar effective temperatures, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_*$</tex>, of 30–60 kK and free–free radiation from the stellar wind with an electron temperature, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm e}$</tex>, of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>15 kK. However, these calculated spectra show an excess at cm wavelength compared with the cm data for almost all stars. This may be interpreted by an infrared excess flux possibly due to the clumping of the stellar wind gas. Assuming an “enhancement factor” that depends on the distance from the center of the stars as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim r^{-\omega}$</tex>, we can reproduce both our near-infrared spectra and the cm data by this clump-corrected free–free radiation with mass-loss rates similar to those derived by Nugis et al. On the other hand, we also estimated the mass-loss rates from our He I 1.083 and He II 1.012 fluxes without a consideration of clumping, although a more detailed consideration should be necessary in order to estimate more reliable values of the mass-loss rates from the He line fluxes.

articleTitle: Discovery of a WZ Sge-Type Dwarf Nova, SDSS J102146.44+234926.3: Unprecedented Infrared Activity during a Rebrightening Phase
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Several SU UMa-type dwarf novae and WZ Sge-type stars tend to exhibit rebrightenings after superoutbursts. The rebrightening phenomenon is problematic for the disk instability theory of dwarf novae, since it requires a large amount of remnant matter in the disk, even after superoutbursts. Here, we report on our optical and infrared observations during the first-ever outburst of a new dwarf nova, SDSS J102146.44+234926.3. During the outburst, we detected superhumps with a period of 0.056281<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.000015 d, which is typical for superhump periods in WZ Sge stars. In conjunction with the appearance of a long-lived rebrightening, we concluded that the object is a new member of WZ Sge stars. Our observations, furthermore, revealed infrared behaviors for the first time in the rebrightening phase of WZ Sge stars. We discovered prominent infrared superhumps. We calculated the color temperature of the infrared superhump source to be 4600–6400 K. These temperatures are too low to be explained by a fully ionized disk appearing during dwarf-nova outbursts. We also found a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{s}$</tex>-band excess over the hot disk component. These unprecedented infrared activities provide evidence for the presence of mass reservoir at the outermost part of the accretion disk. We propose that a moderately high mass-accretion rate at this infrared active region leads to the long-lived rebrightening observed in SDSS J102146.44+234926.3.

articleTitle: Non-LTE Calculation for the Be Star Decretion Disk
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The non-LTE state of the hydrogen gas in isothermal transonic decretion disks around a B1V star has been calculated by an iterative method in order to explore the basic physical process in the disk. This dynamical model is characterized by a density law in the equatorial plane of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho(R) \propto R^{-3.5}$</tex>. The continuous radiation was calculated with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex> iteration in the integral form, while we adopted a single-flight escape probability for lines. We describe the non-LTE state, the radiation flow and conversion in the disk. We conclude that the stellar Balmer continuum plays a key role in the non-LTE state of the disk. An examination of the local energy gain and loss suggests that the disk temperature has double minima along the equatorial plane in the optically thick case: the intermediate region caused by deficient ultraviolet radiation and the outer Lyman <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> cooling region. We also calculated some observable quantities, such as the spectral energy distribution, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$UBV$</tex> colors, the infrared excess and the Balmer line profiles. Our calculations with a mass-loss rate less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{-10}M_{\odot}\ {\rm yr}^{-1}$</tex> reproduce the observed continuum quantities. However, we could not obtain the large H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission strength observed in Be stars. We suggest that the density gradient of the Be star disk is slower than that of an isothermal decretion disk.

articleTitle: Suzaku Detection of Extended/Diffuse Hard X-Ray Emission from the Galactic Center
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Five on-plane regions within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.8D of the galactic center were observed with the Hard X-ray Detector (HXD) and the X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) aboard Suzaku. From all regions, significant hard X-ray emission was detected with HXD-PIN up to 40keV, in addition to the extended plasma emission which is dominant in the XIS band. The hard X-ray signals are inferred to come primarily from a spatially extended source, rather than from a small number of bright discrete objects. Contributions to the HXD data from catalogued X-ray sources, typically brighter than 1mCrab, were estimated and removed using information from Suzaku and other satellites. Even after this removal, the hard X-ray signals remained significant, exhibiting a typical 12-40keV surface brightness of 4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-10}$</tex>ergcm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex>s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>deg<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex> and power-law-like spectra with a photon index of 1.8. Combined fittings to the XIS and HXD-PIN spectra confirm that a separate hard tail component is superposed onto the hot thermal emission, confirming a previous report based on the XIS data. Over the 5-40keV band, the hard tail is spectrally approximated by a power law of photon index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>2, but better by those with somewhat convex shapes. Possible origins of the extended hard X-ray emission are discussed.

articleTitle: Absolute Photometric Calibration of the Infrared Camera (IRC) aboard AKARI
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The absolute photometric calibration of imaging observations with the Infrared Camera (IRC) aboard the AKARI satellite was performed by monitoring the same stars regularly and by observing a set of standard stars. By our monitoring observations, we confirmed that all channels of the IRC were stable to within 4% and that their sensitivities were constant until the liquid helium was exhausted. Using the data of these repeated observations, we evaluated the intrinsic errors as a function of the brightnesses of objects and found that the errors increase rapidly toward fainter objects. We also checked the consistency between short and long exposure times, and confirmed that the data sampling had been executed as designed. Finally, by comparing the estimated in-band flux densities and the observed data values of standard stars, we obtained conversion factors to the absolute flux densities of all the band/exposure configurations. Their absolute uncertainties are estimated to be less than 6%.

articleTitle: Tropospheric Delay Calibrations for VERA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present techniques for the tropospheric delay calibration, which is the key to increasing the accuracy of the phase-referencing astrometry with Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI). We study three methods, and make a comparison of these methods to discuss the accuracy in calibration. Our results show that all three methods can calibrate the tropospheric zenith delay within accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>2cm. We also present simulations of positional errors in VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry (VERA) at the presence of an error in the tropospheric zenith delay, showing that parallax measurements with accuracy of 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>as can be readily achieved for sources at high declination and with small separation angles between the target Galactic maser and extragalactic position references.

articleTitle: Low-Mass Star-Forming Cores in the GF9 Filament
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We carried out an unbiased mapping survey of dense molecular cloud cores traced by the NH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_3$</tex> (1,1) and (2,2) inversion lines in the GF9 filament, which contains an extremely young low-mass protostar, GF9-2 (2006, ApJ, 653, 1369). The survey was conducted using the Nobeyama 45m telescope over a region of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>1.5D<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex> with an angular resolution of 73". The large-scale map revealed that the filament contains at least 7 dense cores, as well as 3 possible ones, located at regular intervals of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>0.9pc. Our analysis shows that these cores have kinetic temperatures of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim$</tex>10K and LTE-masses of 1.8-8.2M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊙</inf>, which makes them typical sites of low-mass star formation. All of the identified cores are likely to be gravitationally unstable, because their LTE-masses are larger than their virial masses. Since the LTE-masses and separations of the cores are consistent with the Jeans masses and lengths, respectively, for the low-density ambient gas, we argue that the identified cores formed via the gravitational fragmentation of the natal filamentary cloud.

articleTitle: Dipolar Oscillations of Stars in General Relativity
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a concise second-order system of ordinary differential equations that describes the adiabatic dipolar oscillation of spherically-symmetric stars in general relativity. The derivation of the system is accomplished by formulating the equations as a Hamiltonian system, and reconsidering a known algebraic relation among the perturbed variables as an integral of the system. The new formulation allows us to examine the structure of eigenfunctions and properties of the eigenfrequency spectrum, so that we can establish a scheme to classify eigenmodes into p-modes and g-modes with mathematical rigorousness. We can also discuss the condition for the existence of dynamically-unstable modes. All of these analyses are totally analogous to those developed in the Newtonian case.

articleTitle: Stellar Parameters and Elemental Abundances of Late-G Giants
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The properties of 322 intermediate-mass late-G giants (comprising 10 planet-host stars) selected as the targets of the Okayama Planet Search Program, many of which are red-clump giants, were comprehensively investigated by establishing their various stellar parameters (atmospheric parameters, including turbulent velocity fields, metallicity, luminosity, mass, age, projected rotational velocity, etc.), and their photospheric chemical abundances for 17 elements, in order to study their mutual dependence, connection with the existence of planets, and possible evolution-related characteristics. The metallicity distribution of planet-host giants was found to be almost the same as that of non-planet-host giants, making marked contrast to the case of planet-host dwarfs tending to be metal-rich. Generally, the metallicities of these comparatively young (typical age of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^{9}$</tex> yr) giants tend to be somewhat lower than those of dwarfs at the same age, and super-metal-rich ([Fe/H] <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 0.2) giants appear to be lacking. Apparent correlations were found between the abundances of C, O, and Na, suggesting that the surface compositions of these elements have undergone appreciable changes due to dredge-up of H-burning products by evolution-induced deep envelope mixing, which becomes more efficient for higher mass stars.

articleTitle: Detection of a Rare Supersoft Outburst Event during a Suzaku Observation of 1E0102.2-7219
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the detection of a transient X-ray source toward the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) using the X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) on board the Suzaku telescope. The source was detected at the edge of the XIS image during a routine observation of the calibration source 1E0102.2-7219, a supernova remnant in the SMC. We constrained the source position using ray-tracing simulations. No such transient source was found at the position in the other Suzaku observations, nor in all of the available archived images of other X-ray missions for the last <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>28 years. The XIS spectrum can be explained by a single blackbody with a temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>72 eV, and an interstellar extinction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>4.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{20}$</tex> H atoms cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex>, consistent with the value to the SMC. An additional absorption edge at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>0.74 keV was also confirmed, which is presumably due to absorption by helium-like oxygen ions. Assuming that the source is at the distance of the SMC, the X-ray luminosity in the 0.2-2.0 keV band is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{37}$</tex> erg s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> and the radius of the source is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{8}$</tex> cm. The XIS light curve shows about a two-fold decline in X-ray flux during the 24 ks observation. Together with the archived data, the X-ray flux in the burst is at least three-orders of magnitude brighter than the undetected quiescent level. All of these properties are often seen among supersoft sources (SSSs). We conclude that the transient source is another example of SSS in the SMC.

articleTitle: The Suzaku Observation of NGC3516: Complex Absorption and the Broad and Narrow FeK Lines
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present results from a 150ks Suzaku observation of the Seyfert 1.5 NGC3516 in 2005 October. The source was in a relatively highly absorbed state. Our best-fit model is consistent with the presence of a low-ionization absorber having a column density near 5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{22}$</tex>cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex> and covering most of the X-ray continuum source (covering fraction 96-100%). A high-ionization absorbing component, which yields a narrow absorption feature consistent with FeXXVIK, is confirmed. A relativistically broadened FeK<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line was required in all fits, even after the complex absorption was taken into account; an additional partial-covering component is an inadequate substitute for the continuum curvature associated with the broad Fe line. A narrow FeK<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> emission line has a velocity width consistent with the Broad Line Region. The low-ionization absorber may be responsible for producing the narrow FeK<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line, though a contribution from additional material out of the line of sight is possible. We include in our model soft band emission lines from He- and H-like ions of N, O, Ne, and Mg, consistent with photo-ionization, though a small contribution from collisionally-ionized emission is possible.

articleTitle: Distance to NGC 281 in a Galactic Fragmenting Superbubble: Parallax Measurements with VERA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have used the Japanese VLBI array VERA to perform high-precision astrometry of an H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex>O maser source in the Galactic star-forming region NGC 281 West, which has been considered to be part of a 300-pc superbubble. We successfully detected a trigonometric parallax of 0.355<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.030mas, corresponding to a source distance of 2.82<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.24kpc. Our direct distance determination of NGC 281 has resolved a large distance discrepancy between previous photometric and kinematic studies; likely NGC 281 is in the far side of the Perseus spiral arm. The source distance as well as the absolute proper motions were used to demonstrate the 3D structure and expansion of the NGC 281 superbubble, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\;$</tex>650pc in size parallel to the Galactic disk and with a shape slightly elongated along the disk or spherical, but not vertically elongated, indicating that the superbubble expansion may be confined to the disk. We estimate the expansion velocity of the superbubble as being <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\;20$</tex>km s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, both perpendicular to and parallel to the Galactic disk with a consistent timescale of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\;20$</tex>Myr.

articleTitle: AKARI IRC Survey of the Large Magellanic Cloud: Outline of the Survey and Initial Results
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed an area of 10deg<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> of the Large Magellanic Cloud using the Infrared Camera (IRC) on board AKARI. The observations were carried out using five imaging filters (3, 7, 11, 15, and 24<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m) and a dispersion prism (2-5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda / \Delta\lambda \sim$</tex> 20) equipped in the IRC. This paper describes an outline of our survey project, and presents some initial results using imaging data that detected over 5.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^5$</tex> near-infrared and 6.4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^4$</tex> mid-infrared point sources. The 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex> detection limits of our survey are about 16.5, 14.0, 12.3, 10.8, and 9.2 in Vega-magnitude at 3, 7, 11, 15, and 24<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m, respectively. The 11 and 15<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m data, which are unique to AKARI IRC, allow us to construct color-magnitude diagrams that are useful to identify stars with circumstellar dust. We found a new sequence in the color-magnitude diagram, which is attributed to red giants with luminosity fainter than that of the tip of the first red-giant branch. We suggest that this sequence is likely to be related to the broad emission feature of aluminum oxide at 11.5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m. The 11 and 15<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m data also indicate that the ([11]-[15]) color of both oxygen-rich and carbon-rich red giants once becomes blue, and then turns red again in the course of their evolution, probably due to a change in the flux ratio of the silicate or silicon carbide emission feature at 10 or 11.3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m to the 15<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m flux.

Author Keywords: stars: AGB and post-AGB-young stellar objects

articleTitle: Probing the Physical Properties of the NGC 5548 Broad Line Region Using Balmer Lines
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigated the physical characteristics of the broad line region (BLR) of NGC 5548 using the Boltzmann plot (BP) method, which we applied to the Balmer lines observed from 1996 to 2004. We found that variability earlier detected in the lines is also present in the temperature parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, obtained from the BP method. Using the BP temperature parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> to calculate temperature, we found that the average temperature for the considered period was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T \approx$</tex>10000 K, and that it varies from 5000K (in 2002) to 15000K (in 1998). This variation correlates with the AGN-component of the optical continuum flux (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r=$</tex> 0.85), and may indicate the existence of an accretion disk in the BLR of NGC 5548.

articleTitle: Distance to VY Canis Majoris with VERA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on astrometric observations of H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex>O masers around the red supergiant VY Canis Majoris carried out with VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry (VERA). Based on astrometric monitoring for 13 months, we successfully measured a trigonometric parallax of 0.88<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.08mas, corresponding to a distance of 1.14<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+0.11} _{-0.09}$</tex>kpc. This is the most accurate determined distance to VY CMa and the first one based on an annual parallax measurement. The luminosity of VY CMa has been overestimated due to a previously accepted distance. With our result, we re-estimated the luminosity of VY CMa to be (3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.5)<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{5}L_{\odot}$</tex> using the bolometric flux integrated over optical and IR wavelengths. This improved luminosity value makes the location of VY CMa on the Hertzsprung-Russell (HR) diagram much closer to the theoretically allowable zone (i.e. the left side of the Hayashi track) than previous ones, though the uncertainty in the effective temperature of the stellar surface still does not permit us to make a final conclusion.

articleTitle: Emergence of a Partially Split Flux Tube into the Solar Atmosphere
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We performed a three-dimensional MHD simulation for the emergence of a partially split flux tube into the solar atmosphere, which was focused on the mechanism of activity observed on the Sun, such as the merging of magnetic polarity regions in the photosphere and the formation of multi-flux domains in the corona. The simulation reproduced that a small polarity region associated with a rotational flow merges into a main polarity region, and the main polarity region later develops a rotational flow in the same direction as the small polarity region. In accordance with the photospheric merging process, multi-flux domains form in the corona and a current layer separating these flux domains travels outward as the flux domains expand. We also investigated the time variations of the magnetic flux, energy, and helicity injected into the atmosphere by the partially split flux tube to see the nature of helicity injection in a multi-pole system.

articleTitle: Suzaku Wide-Band X-Ray Spectroscopy of the Seyfert2 AGN in NGC 4945
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Suzaku observed a nearby Seyfert2 galaxy, NGC 4945, which hosts one of the brightest active galactic nuclei above 20keV. Combining data from the two detectors aboard Suzaku, the AGN intrinsic nuclear emission and its reprocessed signals were observed simultaneously. The intrinsic emission is highly obscured with an absorbing column of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 10^{24}$</tex>cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex>. The spectrum below 10keV is dominated by a reflection continuum and emission lines from neutral/ionized material. Along with a neutral iron K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line, a neutral iron K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> line and a neutral nickel K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line were detected for the first time from this source. The neutral lines and the cold reflection continuum are consistent with both originating in the same location. The Compton down-scattered shoulder in the neutral Fe-K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10\%$</tex> in flux of the narrow core, which confirms that the line originates from reflection, rather than transmission. The flux of the intrinsic emission varied by a factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2$</tex> within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 20$</tex>ks, which requires the obscuring material to be geometrically thin. Broadband spectral modeling showed that the solid angle of the neutral reflector is less than a few <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 10^{-2} \times 2\pi$</tex>. All of this evidence regarding the reprocessed signals suggests that a disk-like absorber/reflector is viewed from a near edge-on angle.

articleTitle: Suzaku Observation of the Metallicity in the Hot Interstellar Medium of the Isolated Elliptical Galaxy NGC 720
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The metal abundances in the interstellar medium of the isolated elliptical galaxy NGC 720 were studied with the CCD X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) aboard the Suzaku satellite. The high detection efficiency along with the excellent spectral resolution of the XIS allowed the K-shell lines of O and Mg to be clearly resolved, and the abundances of O, Ne, Mg, Si, and Fe to be measured with good accuracy for the region within a 3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$'$</tex> radius of NGC 720. The abundances of O and Mg were well determined to be 0.4 and 0.5 solar respectively, meaning stellar metallicity of mass-losing stars in NGC 720 was also well determined. The abundance of Fe was determined to be about 0.7 solar, while the O/Fe, Ne/Fe abundance ratios were found to be about 0.5 and Mg/Fe, Si/Fe were found to be 0.7 in solar units. Relative errors of 30% for the O/Fe, Ne/Fe, Mg/Fe abundance ratios are the lowest among isolated elliptical galaxies so far observed. The higher abundance of Fe than those of O, Ne, and Mg supplied by stellar mass loss indicates that iron is enhanced by SN Ia in NGC 720. These abundance ratios are consistent with those in the ISM of NGC 1399, NGC 1404, and in the ICM of the Fornax cluster observed with Suzaku.

articleTitle: An AKARI Search for Intracluster Dust of Globular Clusters
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on observations of 12 globular clusters with the Far-Infrared Surveyor (FIS) aboard the AKARI satellite. Our goal is to search for emission from cold dust within clusters. We detected diffuse emissions toward NGC6402 and 2808, but the IRAS 100<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m maps show the presence of strong background radiation. They are likely to have been emitted from the Galactic cirrus. We also detected 28 point-like sources mainly in WIDE-S images (90<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu m$</tex>). At least several of them are not associated with clusters, but background galaxies identified in external catalogs. We present the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) by combining near-and-mid infrared data obtained with the Infrared Camera (IRC), if possible. Those SEDs suggest that most of the point sources are background galaxies. For most of the other clusters, we have confirmed a lack of intracluster dust. We evaluated the upper limits of the intracluster dust mass to be between 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-5}$</tex> and 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3}M_{\odot}$</tex>, depending on the dust temperature. The inferred lifetime of the intracluster dust is shorter than 5Myr (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\mathrm{d}}$</tex> = 70K) or 50Myr (35K). Such a short lifetime indicates some mechanism(s) are at work to remove the intracluster dust. We also discuss its impact on the chemical evolution of globular clusters.

articleTitle: Spatial Distributions of Dust and Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons in the Nearby Elliptical Galaxy NGC4589 Observed with AKARI
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on near- to far-infrared (IR) observations of the nearby elliptical galaxy NGC4589 by AKARI. NGC4589 has a complex stellar rotation field with a position angle difference of 45<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\circ}$</tex> between the kinematic and morphological axes, although its morphology shows a smooth optical profile that closely follows the de Vaucouleurs law. The galaxy has a minor-axis dust lane, which is twisted toward the main stellar rotation. These properties strongly support that the galaxy is a relatively old merger remnant. We have obtained the spatial distributions of dust from far-IR emission and near-IR absorption, separately. We have also estimated the distribution of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) from the difference between images in the mid-IR bands. The spatial distributions of the dust and PAHs resemble each other, both showing significant deviations from the smooth stellar distribution. They extend to the main stellar rotation and the direction of the twisted inner dust lane, thus following the relics of the merger. Therefore, a large fraction of the dust and PAHs in NGC4589 are likely to originate from a past merger event.

articleTitle: Mapping Observations of 6.7GHz Methanol Masers with the Japanese VLBINetwork
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have observed 13 methanol maser sources associated with massive star-formingregions: W 3(OH), Mon R2, S 255, W 33A, IRAS 18151-1208, G24.78+0.08, G 29.95-0.02, IRAS18556+0136, W 48, OH 43.8-0.1, ON 1, CepA, and NGC 7538 at 6.7GHz using the Japanese VLBI Network (JVN). Twelve of thethirteen sources were detected at our longest baseline of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>50M<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>, and their imagesare presented. Seven of them are the first VLBI images at 6.7GHz. The highdetection rate and the small fringe spacing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>4 massuggest that most of the methanol maser sources have compact structures. Giventhis compactness as well as the known properties of long life and small internalmotion, the methanol maser line is suitable for astrometry with VLBI.

articleTitle: VERA Observations of SiO Masers in the Symbiotic Star R Aquarii
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present phase-referenced maps of the SiO maser transitions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 1-0 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v =$</tex> 2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J =$</tex> 1-0 from the symbiotic stellar system R Aquarii, which hosts an evolved AGB star plus a hot companion. Observations were performed at two epochs: 2004.98 and 2005.98. Accurate absolute coordinates and proper motions of the emission centroid were obtained; the errors expected for these parameters are also given. We compare the VERA data with the previous astrometry by Hipparcos. This represents a possibility to improve the orbital parameters of the system in a different way than that done before. Thanks to our accurate astrometry, we have also estimated the percentage of spot coincidences between both maser transitions, a parameter that has been proposed to be relevant to discriminate between different maser pumping schemes. Although the overall distributions of both lines are always similar, the spots are rarely coincident, in a percentage ranging between 3% and 20% of the cases. The lack of systematic coincidence favors, in principle, radiative pumping. However, we argue that no firm conclusion can be reached due to a lack of models that include an overlap of rovibrational lines, and that accurately address the coincidence of very intense spots of different maser transitions.

articleTitle: Shock Waves and Line-Profile Variation in roAp Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Line-profile variation of NdIII and PrIII spectrum lines of roAp stars obtained with high spectral resolution and high time resolution seem to be similar to those seen in rapidly rotating B-type line-profile variables: features in the lines appear to move smoothly from blue to red, but return to the blue discontinuously. It has been argued in the past that such behaviour is in disagreement with the oblique-pulsator interpretion of the photometric observations. We point out why that argument is invalid. We propose that the properties of the observed line-profile variation can in principle be explained as a manifestation of a shocked wave train propagating upwards through an acoustically thick layer high in the atmosphere, and demonstrate that it is consistent with the underlying pulsation being an axisymmetric low-degree, probably dipole oscillation more-or-less aligned with the magnetic axis, in accord with the oblique-pulsator model.

articleTitle: ASTE CO(3-2) Observations of the Southern Barred Spiral Galaxy NGC 986: a Large Gaseous Bar Filled with a Dense Molecular Medium
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present CO(3-2) emission observations toward the 3′<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>3′ (or 20kpc<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>20kpc at a distance of 23Mpc) region of the southern barred spiral galaxy NGC 986 using the Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment (ASTE). This effort is a part of our on-going extragalactic CO(3-2) imaging project, ADIoS (ASTE Dense gas Imaging of Spiral galaxies). Our CO(3-2) image revealed the presence of a large (the major axis is 14kpc in total length) gaseous bar filled with a dense molecular medium along the dark lanes observed in optical images. This is the largest “dense-gas rich bar” known to date. The dense gas bar, discovered in NGC 986, could be a huge reservoir of possible “fuel” for future starbursts in the central region, and we suggest that star formation in the central region of NGC 986 could still be in a growing phase. We found a good spatial coincidence between the overall distributions of dense molecular gas traced by CO(3-2) and massive star formation depicted by H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex>. The global CO(3-2) luminosity, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L{'}_{\rm CO(3-2)}$</tex>, of NGC 986 was determined to be (5.4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>1.1)<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^8$</tex>Kkms<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>pc<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex>. The CO(3-2)/CO(1-0) integrated intensity ratio was found to be 0.60<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.13 at a spatial resolution of 44” or 5kpc, and the CO(3-2)/CO(2-1) ratio was 0.67<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex>0.14 at a beam size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>25” or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>2.8kpc. These line ratios suggest moderate excitation conditions of CO lines (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_{\rm H_2}$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim $</tex>10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{3-4}$</tex>cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3}$</tex>) in a few kiloparsec region of central NGC 986.

articleTitle: A Deep Sky Survey of Edgeworth Kuiper Belt Objects with an Improved Shift-and-Add Method
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A survey of the minor bodies in the outer regions of our solar system was carried out using the Suprime-Cam attached to the 8.2 m Subaru Telescope on Mauna Kea on 2001 February 22 and 25. Seven areas, covering a total of 1.4 deg<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> of the sky, were scanned. Five of them were observed with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>-mag limit of approximately 25.0, while the remaining two areas (0.4 deg<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> area of the sky) had a much deeper imaging, reaching an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>-mag limit of 26.0. In order to facilitate our survey, we developed an efficient computer code to detect unknown objects based on an improved shift-and-add method, the validity of which was ascertained from the fact that it could successfully locate the two EKBOs (2001 DM<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{108}$</tex> and 2001 DN<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{108}$</tex>) that had been detected in our preliminary analysis. Using our computer code, we discovered three new EKBOs, viz. 2001 DO<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{108}$</tex>, 2001 DP<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{108}$</tex>, and 2001 DQ<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{108}$</tex>, in addition to 2001 DM<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{108}$</tex> and 2001 DN<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{108}$</tex>. The present survey succeeded in finding a total of 14 EKBOs (five were discovered, and nine were detected) within the 0.4 deg<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> region of the sky observed with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>-mag limit of 26.0.

articleTitle: Colors and Mass-to-Light Ratios of Bulges and Disks of Nearby Spiral Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigated the colors and mass-to-light (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M/L$</tex>) ratios of bulges and disks for 28 nearby spiral galaxies with various morphological types of Sab-Scd, using images in optical and near-infrared (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>) bands as well as published rotation curves. It is shown that the observed colors and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M/L$</tex> values generally agree with the galaxy-formation model with an exponentially declining star-formation rate and a shallow slope initial mass function (e.g., Scalo IMF) for both the bulges and the disks. We find that the bulge <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M/L$</tex> is generally higher than the disk <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M/L$</tex>, and that the galaxies with a larger bulge-to-total luminosity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B/T$</tex>) ratio tend to have a smaller bulge <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M/L$</tex>. This fact indicates that the luminosity-weighted average age of bulges for early-type spirals is younger than that for later-type spirals. These results support a formation scenario that the bulges of middle-type and early-type spirals produce young stars.

articleTitle: Long-Time Simulations of Astrophysical Jets: Energy Structure and Quasi-Periodic Ejection
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have performed self-consistent 2.5-dimensional nonsteady MHD numerical simulations of jet formation as long as possible, including the dynamics of accretion disks. Previous simulations showed that, in the case where the calculation time of the simulations is very short as compared with the time scale of observed jets, there is no significant difference between the characteristics of the nonsteady and steady MHD simulations. Thus, we have investigated long-time evolutions of the mass-accretion rate, mass-outflow rate, jet velocity, and various energy fluxes. We found that the ejection of a jet is quasi-periodic. The period of the ejection, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm ejection}$</tex>, is related to the time needed for the initial magnetic field, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_0$</tex>, to be twisted to generate a toroidal filed, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm ejection} \propto {V_{\rm A}}^{-1} \propto {B_0}^{-1} \propto {E_{\rm mg}}^{-1/2}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\rm A}$</tex> is the Alfvén velocity and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\rm mg}$</tex> the initial magnetic energy. We compared our results with both the steady-state theory and the previous 2.5-dimensional nonsteady MHD simulations. We found that the time-averaged velocity of the jet, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{{\rm jet}, \mathrm{avg}}$</tex>, is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.1V_{\mathrm{K}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.1V_{{\rm jet}, \mathrm{max}}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\mathrm{K}}$</tex> is the Keplerian velocity at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r,{z})=(1,0)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{{\rm jet},\mathrm{max}}$</tex> the maximum velocity of the jet. Nevertheless, the characteristics of our simulations are consistent with those of the steady solution and previous short-time simulations. We found that the dependences of the time-averaged velocity and the mass-outflow rate, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{M}_{{\rm w},\mathrm{avg}}$</tex>, on the initial magnetic field are approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{{\rm jet},\mathrm{avg}} \propto {B_0}^{0.3}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{M}_{{\rm w},\mathrm{avg}} \propto {B_0}^{0.32}$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Suzaku Observations of AWM 7 Cluster of Galaxies: Temperatures, Abundances, and Bulk Motions
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We carried out 3 observations of the cluster of galaxies AWM 7, for the central region and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20'$</tex>-east and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20'$</tex>-west offset regions, with Suzaku. Temperature and abundance profiles were measured out to 27<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$'\simeq$</tex>570<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\;h_{70}^{-1}$</tex>kpc, which corresponded to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>0.35<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{180}$</tex>. The temperature of the intra-cluster medium (ICM) slightly decreased from 3.8keV at the center to 3.4keV in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>0.35<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{180}$</tex> region, indicating a flatter profile than those in other nearby clusters. The abundance ratio of Si to Fe was almost constant in our observations, while the Mg-to-Fe ratio increased with radius from the cluster center. The O to Fe ratio in the west region showed an increase with radius, while that in the east region was almost flat, though the errors were relatively large. These features suggest that the enrichment process is significantly different between products of type II supernovae (O and Mg) and those by type Ia supernovae (Si and Fe). We also examined the positional shift of the central energy of a He-like Fe-K<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line, in search of possible rotation of the ICM. The 90% upper limit for the line-of-sight velocity difference was derived to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta v \lesssim 2000$</tex>kms<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, suggesting that the ellipticity of AWM 7 is rather caused by a recent directional infall of gas along the large-scale filament.

articleTitle: Systematic Infrared 2.5—5μm Spectroscopy of Nearby Ultraluminous Infrared Galaxies with AKARI
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the results of systematic infrared 2.5-5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m spectroscopy of 45 nearby ultraluminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs) at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z <$</tex> 0.3 using AKARI IRC. This paper investigates whether the luminosities of these ULIRGs are dominated by starburst activity, or alternatively, whether optically elusive buried active galactic nuclei (AGNs) are energetically important, based on the strengths of 3.3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission and dust absorption features at 3-4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m. Because of the AKARI IRC's spectroscopic capability in the full 2.5-5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m wavelength range, we can apply this energy diagnostic method to ULIRGs at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z>$</tex> 0.15. We estimate the intrinsic luminosities of extended (several kpc), modestly obscured (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{V} <$</tex> 15mag) starburst activity based on the observed 3.3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m PAH emission luminosities measured in AKARI IRC slitless spectra, and confirm that such starbursts are energetically unimportant in nearby ULIRGs. In roughly half of the observed ULIRGs classified optically as non-Seyferts, we find signatures of luminous buried AGNs. The fraction of ULIRGs with detectable buried AGN signatures increases with increasing infrared luminosity. Our overall results support the scenario that luminous buried AGNs are important in many ULIRGs at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z <$</tex> 0.3 classified optically as non-Seyferts, and that the optical undetectability of such buried AGNs occurs merely because of a large amount of nuclear dust, which can make the sightline of even the lowest dust column density opaque to the ionizing radiation of the AGNs.

articleTitle: Development of Iodine Cells for Subaru HDS and Okayama HIDES. III. AnImprovement on the Radial-Velocity Measurement Technique
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: An improvement of the radial-velocity measurement accuracy is crucial for thedetection of tiny stellar oscillations and exoplanets. Through the analysis ofweek-long extensive observations of solar-type stars (Procyon in 2000, 2002, and2006/2007 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>Cet in 2002 and 2006/2007), we havecarefully examined, revised, and finely tuned the widely used multiple GaussianIP fitting method for the spectrograph, HIDES. By determining a necessary andsufficient number of free parameters in the model as well as introducing aniterative process in the radial-velocity analysis, we can reach a precision ofbelow 3ms<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>, which is much smaller than theprecision of 6ms<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>officially announced so far forHIDES. We also make our technique refined for the 2002 McDonald Procyon data.Even with our revised method, slow radial velocity variations with an amplitudeof about 10ms<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex>are left in the Procyon data. Weemphasize that it is neither due to particular observing instruments norradial-velocity analysis, and thus could be due to stellar origin. The analysispresented here makes the foundations of our next scientific analysis of theradial-velocity variations of Procyon, which will be presented in ourforthcoming papers.

articleTitle: Variable Asymmetry of the Circumstellar Envelope in IK Tauri Traced by SiO Maser Emission
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed the SiO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v=1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v=2$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J=$</tex> 1-0) maser emissions toward the Mira variable IK Tauri (IK Tau, NML Tau, IRC+10050) over nine epochs from 2003 November to 2005 April using the VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry (VERA) telescope array. We found that the SiO maser distributions around IK Tau are highly variable, depending on the stellar pulsation phase. The velocity structures were complex and also time-variable, and are inconsistent with a simply rotating shell that was suggested by previous observations. Based on fittings of the SiO maser distributions to elliptical ring models, we found that the ring size seems to vary in correlation with the pulsation phase, as previously found for TX Cam. Comparisons of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v=1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v=2$</tex> maser distributions reveal that 42-50% of the maser pairs have a positional offset less than 0.5mas, suggesting that the maser pumping in these spots is likely to be dominated by line overlapping or collisional pumping, rather than pure radiative pumping. In order to model the velocity structure of the spoke-like features observed in IK Tau, we propose a ballistic-orbit model, in which a gas clump ejected from the stellar surface moves radially outward with a gravitational deceleration, and argue that the stellar mass can be deduced from that model.

articleTitle: Heavy Element Analysis of X-Ray Faint Elliptical Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Past ASCA and ROSAT observations could not support the general view that elliptical galaxies are sources of metals in the intracluster medium, since observational results have shown that X-ray faint elliptical galaxies exhibit too low metal abundances of hot interstellar medium (ISM). We investigated the radial profiles of the temperature and abundance of 9 X-ray faint elliptical galaxies using the Chandra data. It is found that the heavy element abundance is as high as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>0.7 solar at the central region. Moreover, toward the periphery of galaxies, the metallicity sharply declines. Therefore, the existence of low-metallicity intergalactic gas around X-ray faint elliptical galaxies is indicated. We also investigated the abundance ratios among several elements of 5 X-ray faint elliptical galaxies using the XMM-Newton data, and obtained a hint that the O/Fe ratio of X-ray faint elliptical galaxies is smaller than that of X-ray bright elliptical galaxies. This result perhaps indicates that, in X-ray faint elliptical galaxies, the contribution of SNeIa is smaller than that in X-ray bright ones, and it is speculated that many of the metals in ISM of X-ray faint elliptical galaxies have escaped into the surrounding space.

articleTitle: Spectral Evolution of GRB060904A Observed with Swift and Suzaku- Possibility of Inefficient Electron Acceleration
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed an X-ray afterglow of GRB060904A with the Swift and Suzaku satellites. We found rapid spectral softening during both the prompt tail phase and the decline phase of an X-ray flare in the Swift/BAT and Swift/XRT data. The observed spectra were fit by power-law photon indices which rapidly changed from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma =$</tex> 1.51<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma =$</tex> 5.30<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{+0.69}_{-0.59}$</tex> within a few hundred seconds. This is one of the steepest X-ray spectra ever observed, making it quite difficult to explain by simple electron-acceleration and synchrotron-radiation processes. We then applied an alternative broken power-law with exponential cutoff (BPEC) model. It is valid to consider the exponential shape is equivalent to a synchrotron cutoff. Since the spectral cutoff appears in the soft X-ray band, we conclude that the electron acceleration must be inefficient in the internal shocks of GRB060904A. These cutoff spectra suddenly disappeared at the end of the prompt tail. After that, typical afterglow spectra with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma =$</tex> 2.0 have been continuously and preciously monitored by both Swift/XRT and Suzaku/XIS. We could successfully trace the temporal history of two characteristic break energies that have a time dependence of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\propto t^{-3}$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t^{-4}$</tex>, while the following afterglow spectra are quite stable. This fact indicates that the emitting material of the prompt tail is due to completely different dynamics from the shallow decay component. Therefore, the emission sites of two distinct phenomena obviously differ from each other.

articleTitle: Galaxy Clusters at 0.9 < z < 1.7 in the AKARI NEP Deep Field
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: There is a huge gap between the properties of red-sequence selected massive galaxy clusters at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z<1$</tex> and Lyman-break selected proto-clusters at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z>3$</tex>. It is important to understand when and how the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z>3$</tex> proto-clusters evolve into passive clusters at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z<1$</tex>. We aim to fill this cluster desert by using space-based N4 (4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m) imaging with AKARI. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z'-$</tex> N4 color is a powerful separator of cluster galaxies at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 1, taking advantage of the 4000Å break and the 1.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m bump. We carefully selected 16 promising cluster candidates at 0.9 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> 1.7, which all show an obvious over-density of galaxies and a prominent red-sequence. At this redshift range, the mid-infrared <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{15\mu m}/S_{9\mu m}$</tex> flux ratio is an extinction-free indicator of galaxy star-formation activity due to the redshifted PAH emission lines (6.2, 7.7, and 8.6<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m). We show statistically that the cluster galaxies have a lower <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{15\mu m}/S_{9\mu m}$</tex> flux ratio than do field galaxies, i.e., cluster galaxies already have lower star-formation activity at 0.9 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> 1.7, pushing the formation epoch of these galaxy clusters to a higher redshift.

articleTitle: A Bipolar Outflow of the M-Type Giant IRC −10414 Traced by HO Maser Emission
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on results of five-epoch VLBI observations of H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex>O maser emission in the M-type star IRC -10414, carried out with the VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry (VERA). The maser distribution extends over an area of 70mas<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex>260mas and exhibits a bipolar structure. The relative proper motions of 17 maser features were measured during the monitoring observations spanning nine months.
